blogPosts.title: How Much Does an Electrical Rewire Cost in Chelsea? 2026 Guide
blogPosts.excerpt: Thinking about rewiring your Chelsea home? Discover the average costs, factors that affect price, and how to budget for your electrical upgrade.
body: If your Chelsea home was built before the 1990s, chances are the wiring may need an upgrade. Old rubber-insulated cables, outdated switchboards, and fuse boxes can be a fire risk and may not handle modern power loads. A full rewire is a big job, but it's one of the smartest investments you can make for safety and value.

So what does it cost? For a standard three-bedroom home in Chelsea, expect to pay between $3,500 and $8,000 for a full rewire, depending on accessibility, number of power points, and whether you upgrade the switchboard. Homes with cavity walls are cheaper than those with solid brick or rendered walls where chasing is needed.

Switchboard upgrades alone typically run $800 to $2,000. If you're adding safety switches (RCDs) and surge protection, factor in extra. In Victoria, it's now mandatory to have RCDs on all circuits, so any rewire must include them. We always include this in our quotes for Chelsea jobs.

Other cost drivers include the number of rooms, ceiling heights, and whether you want data cabling or smart home prep. Running separate circuits for air conditioners and ovens adds to the bill but ensures your home doesn't trip. Core Electrical always provides a detailed written quote before work begins.

Timing matters too. Rewiring while you're renovating saves money because walls are open. If you're doing it as a standalone job, we can often complete a full house rewire in three to five days with minimal disruption. We work around your schedule.

Permits and inspections are required for all electrical work in Victoria. As a licensed REC, we handle all paperwork with Energy Safe Victoria. After the rewire, we issue a Certificate of Electrical Safety. Don't risk an unlicensed sparky – the savings aren't worth the danger.

In Chelsea, many older homes near the beach also face corrosion issues in switchboards from salt air. We often replace bus bars and upgrade enclosures to weatherproof types. This adds a little to the cost but prevents future faults.
Ready to book a free quote? Contact Core Electrical for a no-obligation inspection and written estimate. We'll walk you through the process and answer all your questions. Your safety comes first.

blogPosts.title: Benefits of Home Automation for Bayside Homes
blogPosts.excerpt: Discover how C-BUS and smart home technology can save energy, boost security, and make daily life easier for Chelsea and Bayside homeowners.
body: Home automation isn't just for new builds. More and more Chelsea and Bayside homeowners are retrofitting smart systems to improve comfort and control. With Clipsal C-BUS, you can manage lighting, blinds, heating, and security from a single touchscreen or your phone.

Why go smart? First, energy savings. Automated lighting and motorised blinds respond to the sun's position, reducing heat gain in summer and keeping warmth in during winter. You can schedule lights to turn off when rooms are empty. Over a year, this cuts your power bill noticeably.

Security is another big draw. Integrate your alarm system with C-BUS so that setting the alarm also shuts off lights and locks blinds. You can simulate occupancy when you're away – perfect for holiday peace of mind. Core Electrical installs cameras and intercoms that work with your automation system.

Installation in existing homes is simpler than you think. Many C-BUS keypads and dimmers fit into standard wall boxes, so no major rewiring is needed. Our team will assess your current wiring and recommend the most efficient upgrade path. We've retrofitted dozens of homes in Chelsea and Aspendale.

For new builds, we can design a full automation package from scratch. Pre-wire for future expansion, run data cables to every window for automated blinds, and plan the perfect lighting scenes. We work with architects and builders to integrate seamlessly.

What does it cost? A basic automation system for lighting and blinds starts around $2,500 for a small home. A fully integrated system with climate control, security, and audio can run $10,000–$20,000. We provide itemised quotes so you see where every dollar goes.

Before you commit, think about what you actually need. Most homeowners start with lighting and blinds, then add security later. C-BUS is modular, so you can expand without ripping out old gear. We'll help you prioritise.
Talk to us for a free consultation. Whether you're building new or retrofitting, Core Electrical has the experience to make your home smarter, safer, and more efficient.

blogPosts.title: Why Choose LED Lighting for Your Melbourne Home?
blogPosts.excerpt: LED lighting is the future. We break down the benefits – lower bills, longer life, better light – and why every Chelsea home should make the switch.
body: If you're still using halogen or incandescent bulbs in your Chelsea home, you're spending more than you need to. LED lighting uses up to 80% less energy and lasts 25 times longer. Over the life of a single LED bulb, you can save $100 or more in electricity and replacement costs.

The quality of LED light has improved enormously. You can now choose warm white (2700K) for a cosy feel or cool white (4000K) for kitchens and workspaces. Dimmable LEDs work with most existing dimmer switches, though older dimmers may need upgrading to avoid flickering.

Installation is straightforward for most fittings. Downlights, strip lights under cabinets, and outdoor floodlights all have LED options. Core Electrical can retrofit your entire home in a day, replacing downlight globes or upgrading whole fittings. We use high-quality brands like Philips and Osram.

In addition to energy savings, LEDs produce very little heat. This reduces load on your air conditioning in summer – a double saving. They're also safer because they don't get hot enough to start a fire. For homes with young children or pets, this is a real peace of mind.

Melbourne's climate can be tough on outdoor lighting. Rain, heat, and salty air near Chelsea beach can corrode metal fittings. Look for LEDs with IP65 rating for outdoor use. We recommend stainless steel or marine-grade fixtures for coastal homes.

What about the upfront cost? LEDs cost more than halogens initially, but you recoup that within a year or two. With prices dropping, a 10-pack of quality LEDs is now under $30. The long-term savings are undeniable.
Rebates? The Victorian Energy Upgrades program may offer discounts on LED installation for eligible households. We can advise on what's available and help you claim the rebate. It's a no-brainer.
Ready to brighten your home and lower bills? Call Core Electrical for a free lighting audit. We'll recommend the best LED solutions for your Chelsea property and give you a fixed quote. Simple.

blogPosts.title: Electrical Safety Tips for Renovations in Chelsea
blogPosts.excerpt: Planning a renovation? Don't forget the electrical side. Safety, compliance, and smart planning are crucial for any Chelsea home improvement project.
body: Renovating a home in Chelsea? Whether you're knocking down walls, extending a kitchen, or converting a garage, electrical work must be done safely and to code. In Victoria, all electrical installations must comply with AS/NZS 3000 (the Wiring Rules).

First, never attempt DIY electrical work. It's illegal and dangerous. Only a licensed electrician can legally connect or alter fixed wiring. We've seen too many Chelsea homeowners try to save a few dollars and end up with unsafe circuits or fines from inspectors.

Second, plan ahead. Involve your electrician early in the renovation design. Want extra power points for a kitchen island? Under-cabinet lighting? Electric oven? Running cables is much easier when walls are open. Retrofits cost more and may require chasing into plaster.

Third, consider upgrading your switchboard. Older homes may still have ceramic fuses or no safety switches. A modern switchboard with RCDs and surge protection is essential – and often required by law when you renovate. It protects both your family and your appliances.

Fourth, think about future needs. Pre-wire for solar panels, electric vehicle charging, or home automation even if you don't install them now. Running a spare conduit from the switchboard to the garage costs little during a renovation but saves thousands later.

For bathrooms, special rules apply. All power points must be at least 1.5 metres from water sources. Lighting must be IP-rated for moisture. Underfloor heating needs its own circuit. We handle all the compliance to pass inspection.

Finally, get everything documented. Your electrician should provide a Certificate of Electrical Safety for any new work. This is needed when you sell the house. Core Electrical provides full documentation and testing.
